score_rationale.accuracy: English and grammar explanations are correct, but online quiz q8 offers 'I am a cook' as a distractor even though it is an equally valid translation, and there are a few small Spanish nits.
score_rationale.level_fit: Most lines are short A1 chunks, but Listening 2 ('I have to go', 'When will they see each other again?') is above a first-lesson level.
score_rationale.scaffolding: Listening 2 and the in-person quiz require untaught words (nurse, son, next Saturday, waiter) and third-person 'She is' to answer, in the very first lesson.
score_rationale.timing: The agenda adds up to exactly 120 minutes with no slack for welcome or wrap-up, and 14 vocabulary chunks in 15 minutes is tight for absolute beginners.
score_rationale.tutor_usability: Mostly runnable from the page, though the role-play 'Rosa' identity is confusing and a different Rosa appears in Listening 2.
score_rationale.relevance_sensitivity: Practical, everyday introductions; the graded self-questions about origin and job have no made-up-persona option, which can be uncomfortable for recent migrants without work.

findings.issue: 'I am a cook' is also a correct English rendering of 'Trabajo como cocinero', but the auto-graded quiz marks it wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the distractor 'I am a cook' with a clearly wrong option such as 'I am from a cook' or 'I cook as a work'.
findings.verifier_reason: Q8 is an auto-graded multiple-choice item whose options include 'I am a cook', a natural and accurate English rendering of 'Trabajo como cocinero', but the key accepts only 'I work as a cook', so there are two defensible answers and the key is too narrow for the student app.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 2: Talking About Work, question 2 (l2q2)
findings.quote: I work as a nurse at a hospital.
findings.issue: The answer to l2q2 ('She is a nurse.') depends on 'nurse' (and 'hospital'), which are not taught in lesson 01, and on third-person 'She is', which is not taught either.
findings.suggested_fix: Have Rosa say 'I work as a cook.' (taught) and key l2q2 as 'A cook' / 'She works as a cook'; accept short answers.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 2: Talking About Work, question 3 (l2q3)
findings.quote: My son is 8 years old and my daughter is 12.
findings.issue: l2q3 depends on 'son'/'daughter'/'children', which are untaught; the exchange also models asking about family in a lesson about introducing yourself.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace with taught language, e.g. Mr. Kim: 'How old are you, Rosa?' Rosa: 'I am thirty-five years old.' and key l2q3 'How old is Rosa?' -> '35 (years old)'.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 2: Talking About Work, question 4 (l2q4)
findings.quote: When will they see each other again?
findings.issue: The question uses untaught 'will' and 'each other', and the answer 'Next Saturday' depends on untaught 'next' and days of the week.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop l2q4 or replace it with a taught item, e.g. 'What does Rosa say at the end?' -> 'Goodbye! See you later.'

findings.issue: The answer needs 'waiter', which is never taught (the lesson only teaches 'cook'); the key also omits valid 'I am a waiter' / 'server'.
findings.suggested_fix: Use 'Trabajo como cocinero.' -> 'I work as a cook.', or add 'waiter' to vocab; accept 'I am a waiter/server' too.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 2: Talking About Work, question 1 (l2q1)
findings.issue: Key expects full third-person sentences ('She is fine.', also l2q2 'She is a nurse.') though 'she is' is untaught; a beginner answering 'Fine' or 'I am fine' could be marked wrong by a volunteer reading the key.
findings.suggested_fix: Key short answers: 'Fine (She is fine.)'; add a tutor note that one-word answers are correct. Also in l2q2.

findings.quote: I work as a ___. (Answers will vary.)
findings.issue: Graded self-questions (iq9 origin, iq10 job) assume the learner has a job and require real personal answers; recent migrants may be unemployed or uneasy discussing work, and no made-up option is offered.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a note: 'You can answer about yourself or about a made-up person (e.g. Carmen from Honduras, a cook).' and accept 'I am looking for work.' Also in iq9 and Role-play Part 3 'Practice describing your job'.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 2: Talking About Work
findings.quote: Nice! Well, I have to go. See you later!
findings.issue: Background script includes untaught chunks ('I have to go', 'Well', 'That is great', 'Very good') that a first-lesson learner has not seen.
findings.suggested_fix: Simplify to 'Goodbye, Rosa! See you later!'; replace 'That is great' with 'Nice!'.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Role-play: Part 2: Sharing more about yourself
findings.issue: Role-play and practice lines use untaught content words ('languages', 'now', 'too' in Part 1, 'neighbor' in Guided practice); no graded answer depends on them.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'language' and 'neighbor' to vocab or rephrase: 'Do you speak English?' -> 'I speak Spanish and a little English.'

findings.section: Tutor slides › Listening 1: Meeting at the Community Center, question 1 (l1q1)
findings.issue: Question uses untaught 'woman' and possessive 's (also 'Where does Luis live now?' uses third-person 'does'); the Spanish prompt helps, so answers don't depend on it.
findings.suggested_fix: Rephrase as 'What is her name? (Ana / Luis?)' or keep and have the tutor point to the Spanish prompt.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Role-play: Part 1: Meeting someone new
findings.issue: Awkward Spanish for 'Nice to meet you too'; native speakers say 'Igualmente' or 'El gusto es mío'.
findings.suggested_fix: Change to 'Igualmente.' or 'El gusto es mío.'

findings.section: Tutor slides › Guided practice: Say It Right
findings.issue: Missing accent in the Spanish name 'María' (inconsistent with the vocab example).
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'Me llamo María.'; also in Student app › Homework worksheet, item 1 (w1) promptEs.

findings.section: Tutor slides › Role-play: Part 2: Sharing more about yourself
findings.quote: Rosa keeps talking. Practice sharing where you are from and what you speak.
findings.issue: In Part 1 the student says 'My name is Rosa', so 'Rosa keeps talking' is confusing about who Rosa is; a different Rosa (a nurse with children) then appears in Listening 2.
findings.suggested_fix: Write 'The conversation continues. Practice sharing...' and rename the Listening 2 character (e.g. 'Carmen').

findings.issue: 14 vocabulary entries (several of them paired, like this one) in 15 minutes, and an agenda that totals exactly 120 minutes with no time for welcome or wrap-up, is tight for absolute beginners.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a tutor note marking optional items (e.g. Listening 2, Guided practice 'Say It Right') to skip if time runs short.
